title: Peak season: measure which WhatsApp campaign sells, then double down
summary: Buen Fin, Black Friday and the holidays are when you send the most messages. Boom templates now add UTM tags to their buttons, so every visit reaches your analytics with its campaign and you know what to repeat.
body_markdown:
Peak season is coming. Between Buen Fin, Black Friday and the holidays you'll send more WhatsApp campaigns than in the rest of the year, and each one competes for the same attention. The question that matters isn't how many messages went out, it's **which one brought sales** . Until now that was hard to answer: visits from a WhatsApp button showed up in Google Analytics or Shopify as direct traffic, with no campaign.


WhatsApp templates you create in Boom now **add UTM tags to their buttons** . Every visit arrives with` utm_source=boom` ,` utm_medium=whatsapp` and the campaign name. What you can measure, you can improve: you see which message works and put more behind it.


## How it works


Go to **Templates › WhatsApp** and use **Create Template** . Choose **Call to Action** or **Card** and add a button of type **URL** . Type your link as usual, for example` https://yourstore.com/black-friday` .


Right under the buttons you'll see **Tag links for analytics** , already ticked, next to the campaign name. Under each link you'll see the tags it will carry. There's nothing else to do.


The default tags are:


- ` utm_source=boom`
- ` utm_medium=whatsapp`
- ` utm_campaign` = the template's name, lowercased, with` _` instead of spaces


Use **Customize** to change the source, medium or campaign. Empty fields use the defaults.


## Measure every campaign and repeat the one that sells


Because the campaign takes the template's name, **one template per campaign** gives you one row per campaign in your analytics. For peak season:


1. **Name your templates after your campaigns** , for example` buen_fin_discount` and` buen_fin_free_shipping` , and send each one to part of your audience.
2. **Compare them in your analytics** : sessions, carts and sales by` utm_campaign` .
3. **Double down on the winner.** Send it to the rest of your audience and use it as the starting point for Black Friday.


It also works with links that change per customer. If your button ends in a variable, like an abandoned-cart link (` https://yourstore.com/{{2}}` ), Boom adds the tags to each customer's link when the message is sent. Now you know how many carts WhatsApp brings back.


## Change the tags anytime


The tags are added when each message is sent; they aren't part of what WhatsApp reviews. So you can change them later: open the template and use **Edit** on the **Link tracking** card. The change applies to the next messages, **with no new WhatsApp review** .


What you can't do is turn tags on for a template WhatsApp already approved, because that would change the link it reviewed. For an older template, create a new one with tags on.


## Good to know


- **If your link already has its own UTM tags** , we keep yours and add nothing.
- **If it has a` #` section** , like` yourstore.com/product#reviews` , the link is sent untagged: anything after` #` never reaches your site. The form tells you.
- **Cookies come first.** If your site asks visitors to accept cookies, Google Analytics and similar tools record the visit and its campaign only after the visitor accepts, as with any other campaign.


## From the API and MCP


When you create a template with` POST /api/v1/templates` , add` "tracking": { "utm": {} }` for the default tags, or set` source` ,` medium` or` campaign` . Without` tracking` , the template is created untagged. To change them later, use` PATCH /api/v1/templates/{id}/tracking` or the MCP tool` templates_tracking_update` .


## Live now


Tags are available to every workspace, on every new template with link buttons. They're added to buttons only, not to links you write inside the message text. The[docs](https://docs.useboom.ai/whatsapp-link-tracking) have the details.
